description: Recovery from a kill during implementation, on build task f-comment-edit (row F): killed at the second source edit under src/app/, then resumed in a fresh process.
notes: Copy of build task f-comment-edit (ticket, hidden tests, reference patch, setup). Kill point: the 2nd stream line carrying an Edit, MultiEdit or Write tool call whose file_path is under src/app/ (the application code the ticket changes; tests live under src/tests/). nth=2 means the first source edit has already run, so the tree is partly implemented; the second may or may not land before the kill (the line is emitted before the tool runs). Why it marks the phase for both arms: native edits src/app/ only while implementing, in its one process. Daedalus's step 1 (/daedalus:feature-plan) is PLAN mode and writes only docs/plans/, so its first src/app/ edits come from the implementer subagent inside step 2 (/daedalus:project-manager); the match relies on subagent tool calls appearing in the parent's stream-json with parent_tool_use_id [verify in T0]. If they don't, the Daedalus arm is never killed (recovery.killed_at null, success null). Edits made through Bash (sed -i, heredocs) aren't seen. The pattern expects file_path inside the tool input object; other input keys may come first. Resume: one fresh process whose prompt points to the run's ticket file ({ticket_path}, the ticket delivered as data, as in the arms' own prompts), a note that the earlier session was interrupted, the arm's resume_hint (Daedalus: continue /daedalus:project-manager on its plan if docs/plans/<slug>.md exists; native: none) and the shared non-interactive instruction. Success = hidden tests pass at the end. budget_usd is a placeholder; the harness reserves twice the cap for recovery runs.
